contexts.text: Conscience is their plane...
In a horizontal plane, and in a vertical one...
(The formation of three planes in man.)
Freedom the plane of reception...
(The good of infancy is the plane for the good of wisdom.) AC 2306.
Erroneous things serve for ultimate planes.
The plane itself into which that light can operate... is the good of faith; thus conscience.
Honour, decorum, etc., are planes with man upon which conscience is founded; and, consequently, intelligence and wisdom...
In these there is no plane...
Man is first introduced into innocence in order that it may be a plane for all the other states.
The spiritual life is terminated in the natural as in an ultimate plane...
In the other life man has with him his natural affections, doctrinals, and scientifics... for these are the planes in which his interiors are terminated...
All situations there are determined... according to planes; as, in the plane of the head, etc. AC 4321:2.
The natural memory serves Spirits and Angels as a plane...
The sense of the letter serves the internal sense as a plane...

If there is not some recipient of good and truth, as a soil, or plane, in the interior man which lives after death, the influent good and truth cannot be received; and therefore man, while he lives in the world, ought to be solicitous to procure for himself interiorly such a plane... This plane is acquired through charity towards the neighbour... This plane is what is called conscience...
The Spiritual Kingdom is as a plane to the Celestial.

There are in man two planes upon which are founded the Celestial and spiritual things which come from the Lord. The one plane is interior, and the other exterior. The planes themselves are nothing else than conscience. Without the planes... nothing celestial and spiritual from the Lord can be fixed: it Hows through like water through a sieve: and therefore those devoid of such a plane do not know what conscience is. (Continued. See Conscience.) AC 5145:4. AC 6207.
These three planes act as a one with the regenerate; for the one inflows into the other...
With those of the representative Church, externals served as a plane...
The Natural must be the plane...
Sensuous scientifics serve as planes for the Knowledges of spiritual things.
Spirits known from their plane. Enumerated.
The natural memory is there as a fundamental plane, into which interior truths and goods fall; and if this plane is not receptible of (them), they are extinguished, perverted, or rejected.
In the plane of the sole of the foot.
Still the genuine face is as a plane...
Into innocence as into a plane inflow love and charity from the Lord.
Therefore with them there is no plane into which Heaven can operate; but whatever inflows from Heaven, flows through; and, when it comes into the natural man, it is not received there...
The Angels then have a plane (in the man) into which they operate...
The interiors of the Natural, man carries with him into the other life, where they serve as a plane for spiritual and celestial things. Explained.
The things which inflow through the externa ay, are (really) called forth by the internal man, to serve as a plane for the celestial and spiritual things which inflow through the internal way.
When the degrees are terminated... every degree is a plane, in which rests... the good which inflows from the Lord. (Continued. See Degree, and Terminate.)
Without such a plane (as is formed by sensuous things in the exterior Natural) a man in the body cannot think about the things which are above sensuous things. Explained.
The speech of words is the plane in which is the meaning.
Therefore this plane (the exterior Natural) is the first formed.
From the plane of the septum of the nose towards the plane of the left ear.
The internal sense serves as a plane (to the affections of love and charity of the Inmost Heaven).
The Natural is the plane in which the influx terminates; and therefore unless the Natural... becomes nothing, good cannot inflow. AC 6406.
When the understanding has been formed, scientifics form an ultimate plane, in which the man thinks no longer; but above it. AC 6007.

(Thus) the truths of faith, inrooted by the affection of truth, are the plane into which the Angels operate; and therefore those who have not this plane cannot be led by the Angels... for the operation of the Angels... passes through. But this plane cannot be acquired unless the truths of faith have been put into act... AC 6207. AC 6208. AC 6213.
The progression takes place in order, from exteriors to interiors... for exteriors then serve as a plane for interiors.
Such doctrinals, being the first which man learns, then serve him as an ultimate plane.
(In embryos), one part is always a plane for another.
Into these (external) bonds, which make the ultimate plane, the Lord then inflows... But this plane is nothing in the other life...
In the plane of the lower chest.
The prior state then serves as a plane for the following one; and so continually.
Scientifics must first be learned, because they are a plane for the things of the understanding... (Thus) the Scientific is the first plane when man is being regenerated. AC 6751.
That the Scientific was also the first plane with the Lord...

When man is being regenerated, the generals of faith, or the rudiments of the doctrine of the Church, are the first plane; then come the particulars of doctrine; afterwards, successively, things more interior. These planes are what are illustrated by the light of Heaven. Hence is the Intellectual, and the Perceptive...
The Divine influx (then) inflows into the interior plane into which the man has been elevated.
These emissaries appear... in planes from the head down to the soles of the feet.
A little above the plane of the head.
(The successive [planes] of creation.)
The planet Mars appears... in the plane of the breast.
The good which is formed through the truths of faith is the plane into which Heaven can inflow...
Through the good of the Church is formed conscience, which is the plane into which the Angels inflow... whereas through natural good not any plane can be formed for the Angels.
The part of the face devoid of life (is) for a plane interiorly...
After regeneration... the delight of pleasures serves for... an ultimate plane, in which spiritual good... is terminated.
At last (these things) become the ultimate planes of celestial good.
They cannot be saved, because they have no plane into which Heaven can inflow... for conscience is the plane and receptacle of the influx of Heaven.
The regeneration of man in the world is only a plane for the perfecting of his life to eternity.
To these three things the speech of man serves for an ultimate plane.
This state (of external innocence) is the plane of the new life when the man is being regenerated...
This good inflows with infants, that it may serve in advancing age... for a plane to receive truths AC 10134:2.
A prior state is a plane for the following ones, continually.
This (ultimate) Sensuous is the ultimate plane in which the life of man is terminated, and Upon which it reposes...
Such as is the quality of the natural man when he dies, such he remains... for this is the plane into which the interior things inflow. Explained.
The Spirits (of the Third Earth) appear in the plane of the head...
By the interior things of worship the man of the Church communicates with the Heavens, to which the external [thereof] serves as a plane upon which the interior things stand...
I seemed to be elevated from the horizontal plane.
The innocence of infants is the plane of all the affections of good and truth.

Those who die as adults have acquired a plane from the material world, and take it with them. This plane is their memory and its corporeal natural affection. This remains fixed, and is quiescent; but still it serves their thought after death for an ultimate plane; for the thought inflows into it. Hence it is that such as is this plane, and such as is the correspondence of the Rational with the things which are there, such is the man after death. But those who die as infants... have not such a plane; but a spiritual natural plane... and therefore they cannot be in such gross affections and thoughts.
The planes of this light, in which come forth the variegations as of colours, are the interiors of the mind.
Conjugial love is the very plane of the Divine influx. Explained. HH 371.

The reason man cannot be reformed after death by instruction, is that the ultimate plane, which consists of natural Knowledges and affections, is then quiescent, and cannot be opened, because it is not spiritual; and, upon this plane, the interior things of the mind rest...
There is a general likeness, from which, as from a plane of derivation, the several faces have some likeness.
Out of man's will they make as it were an oval plane; and (affirm) that when the operation of the Holy Spirit approaches this plane, it deflects itself... TCR 462.
(These spheres) meet in the rational plane with man; which is intermediate between Heaven and Hell.
For the ultimate plane, in which the delights of both (conjugial and scortatory love) cease... is the same.
That which is in the memory from parents and masters then serves (the understanding) for a plane.

The reason man progresses (from corporeal to sensuous, natural, rational, and spiritual) is that planes may be formed, on which the higher things may rest... The ultimate plane... may be likened to the soil...
As this is the ultimate plane (of the love of the sex)...
Concerning a certain plane in man, as to his affections. Explained.
The quarters... in the plane of the head, etc.
Which is the first plane... SE 3393.
Concerning inauguration into the first plane, or first faculty...
Natural and corporeal things are the planes of their thought.
How a plane of ideas, in which order is terminated, is formed in this world, and in this world only. SE 4038.
The vessels of the memory are planes in which ideas are determined...
The memory of man is their ultimate plane.
That the worst men may have a plane to receive the truths of faith.
As the ultimate plane is with man, in his affections...
Because man is the ultimate plane.
For they have no plane...
Hence it is evident that a plane ought to be formed from the truths of faith, or from the Knowledges of good and truth in both doctrine and life...
All (in the World of Spirits) when taken together, are not extended into a plane; but into a globe...

Hence while man lives here he acquires a fixed plane, which cannot be changed after death... This plane he has with him, but it is altogether quiescent; but still his interior things cease in it. Unless it has correspondence with the internal things with him, it cannot be well with him...
Man's natural thought is the plane in which cease all things of angelic wisdom... Into this plane fall all things which the Angels think. Hence, such as is the plane, such is their wisdom...
This plane and ultimate is with an intelligent man, whether he is thinking about such things, or about other things, or whether he is sleeping...
Many men together may serve as one plane for one Angel. The Lord so disposes that what is wanting in one is in the other...

The first plane is the inmost of the Rational... The second plane is the middle of the Rational... The third plane is that of the conscience of what is just and right... The fourth plane is that of honourableness and decorum... These planes can be conjoined, and the interior inflow into the exterior; and then the last plane, namely, that of honourableness and decorum, is good...
But when the exterior plane is separated from the interior... it is only simulatory...
All spiritual things cease in natural ones; for in these they have their ultimate plane...
